claim: Quinidine has been used as an anticonvulsant to treat patients with KCNT1-related epilepsy by targeting gain-of-function KCNT1 pathogenic mutant variants.
source: Quinidine has been used as an anticonvulsant to treat patients with KCNT1-related epilepsy by targeting gain-of-function KCNT1 pathogenic mutant variants.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing quinidine's clinical use in KCNT1-related epilepsy.

claim: The detailed mechanism underlying quinidine's blockade against KCNT1 (Slack) remains elusive.
source: However, the detailed mechanism underlying quinidine's blockade against KCNT1 (Slack) remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: NaV1.6 binds to Slack.
source: Here, we report a functional and physical coupling of the voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.6 and Slack. NaV1.6 binds to and highly sensitizes Slack to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation and FRET assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: NaV1.6 highly sensitizes Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: NaV1.6 binds to and highly sensitizes Slack to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing nearly 100-fold sensitization in IC50 values.

claim: Homozygous knockout of NaV1.6 reduces the sensitivity of native sodium-activated potassium currents to quinidine blockade.
source: Homozygous knockout of NaV1.6 reduces the sensitivity of native sodium-activated potassium currents to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from primary cortical neurons of NaV1.6 knockout mice.

claim: NaV1.6-mediated sensitization requires the involvement of NaV1.6's N- and C-termini binding to Slack's C-terminus.
source: NaV1.6-mediated sensitization requires the involvement of NaV1.6's N- and C-termini binding to Slack's C-terminus and is enhanced by transient sodium influx through NaV1.6.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation, GST pull-down assays, and functional studies with NaV1.6 fragments.

claim: NaV1.6-mediated sensitization is enhanced by transient sodium influx through NaV1.6.
source: NaV1.6-mediated sensitization requires the involvement of NaV1.6's N- and C-termini binding to Slack's C-terminus and is enhanced by transient sodium influx through NaV1.6.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using TTX to block sodium influx and riluzole to selectively block persistent sodium currents.

claim: Disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction by viral expression of Slack's C-terminus can protect against SlackG269S-induced seizures in mice.
source: Moreover, disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction by viral expression of Slack's C-terminus can protect against SlackG269S-induced seizures in mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vivo seizure susceptibility studies using AAV-mediated gene delivery.

claim: Slack channels are encoded by the KCNT1 (SLO2.2) gene.
source: Slack channels encoded by the KCNT1 (SLO2.2) gene are gated by Na+, while Slick channels encoded by the KCNT2 (SLO2.1) gene are more sensitive to Cl- than Na+.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the genetic basis of Slack channels.

claim: Slack channels are gated by Na+.
source: Slack channels encoded by the KCNT1 (SLO2.2) gene are gated by Na+, while Slick channels encoded by the KCNT2 (SLO2.1) gene are more sensitive to Cl- than Na+.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Slack channel function.

claim: Slick channels are encoded by the KCNT2 (SLO2.1) gene.
source: Slack channels encoded by the KCNT1 (SLO2.2) gene are gated by Na+, while Slick channels encoded by the KCNT2 (SLO2.1) gene are more sensitive to Cl- than Na+.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the genetic basis of Slick channels.

claim: Slick channels are more sensitive to Cl- than Na+.
source: Slack channels encoded by the KCNT1 (SLO2.2) gene are gated by Na+, while Slick channels encoded by the KCNT2 (SLO2.1) gene are more sensitive to Cl- than Na+.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Slick channel function.

claim: Slack channels are expressed at high levels in the central nervous system (CNS), especially the cortex and brainstem.
source: Slack channels are expressed at high levels in the central nervous system (CNS), especially the cortex and brainstem (Joiner et al., 1998; Rizzi et al., 2016; Bhattacharjee et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Slack channel expression patterns.

claim: Activation of Slack channels by intracellular sodium ions forms delayed outward currents in neurons.
source: Activation of Slack channels by intracellular sodium ions forms delayed outward currents in neurons, contributes to slow afterhyperpolarization (AHP) following repeated action potentials, and modulates the firing frequency of neurons (Yang et al., 2007; Wallén et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Slack channel function.

claim: Activation of Slack channels contributes to slow afterhyperpolarization (AHP) following repeated action potentials.
source: Activation of Slack channels by intracellular sodium ions forms delayed outward currents in neurons, contributes to slow afterhyperpolarization (AHP) following repeated action potentials, and modulates the firing frequency of neurons (Yang et al., 2007; Wallén et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Slack channel function.

claim: Activation of Slack channels modulates the firing frequency of neurons.
source: Activation of Slack channels by intracellular sodium ions forms delayed outward currents in neurons, contributes to slow afterhyperpolarization (AHP) following repeated action potentials, and modulates the firing frequency of neurons (Yang et al., 2007; Wallén et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Slack channel function.

claim: Mutations in the KCNT1 gene have been implicated in a wide spectrum of epileptic disorders.
source: Mutations in the KCNT1 gene have been implicated in a wide spectrum of epileptic disorders, including early-onset epilepsy (e.g., epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), non-EIMFS developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, and autosomal-dominant or sporadic sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (ADSHE)) (Heron et al., 2012; Barcia et al., 2012; Kingwell, 2012; Bonardi et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on KCNT1 mutations and epilepsy.

claim: Over 50 mutations related to seizure disorders have been identified in KCNT1.
source: Over 50 mutations related to seizure disorders have been identified, typically displaying a gain-of-function (GOF) phenotype in heterologous expression systems (Bonardi et al., 2021; McTague et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on KCNT1 mutations.

claim: KCNT1 mutations typically display a gain-of-function (GOF) phenotype in heterologous expression systems.
source: Over 50 mutations related to seizure disorders have been identified, typically displaying a gain-of-function (GOF) phenotype in heterologous expression systems (Bonardi et al., 2021; McTague et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on KCNT1 mutations.

claim: Quinidine has emerged as a precision therapy for KCNT1-related epilepsy by blocking Slack mutant variants in vitro.
source: The prescribed antiarrhythmic drug, quinidine, has emerged as a precision therapy for KCNT1-related epilepsy by blocking Slack mutant variants in vitro and conferring decreased seizure frequency and improved psychomotor development in clinical treatment (Milligan et al., 2014; Bearden et al., 2014; Mikati et al., 2015; Numis et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on quinidine therapy.

claim: Quinidine confers decreased seizure frequency and improved psychomotor development in clinical treatment of KCNT1-related epilepsy.
source: The prescribed antiarrhythmic drug, quinidine, has emerged as a precision therapy for KCNT1-related epilepsy by blocking Slack mutant variants in vitro and conferring decreased seizure frequency and improved psychomotor development in clinical treatment (Milligan et al., 2014; Bearden et al., 2014; Mikati et al., 2015; Numis et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on quinidine therapy.

claim: Clinical quinidine therapy has shown limited success and contradictory therapeutic effects.
source: However, clinical quinidine therapy has shown limited success and contradictory therapeutic effects, probably due to poor blood–brain barrier penetration, dose-limiting off-target effects, phenotype–genotype associations, and rational therapeutic schedule (Numis et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2023; Cole et al., 2021; Xu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on quinidine therapy outcomes.

claim: Slack requires high intracellular-free Na+ concentrations ([Na+]in) for its activation in neurons (Kd of ~66 mM).
source: Slack requires high intracellular-free Na+ concentrations ([Na+]in) for its activation in neurons (Kd of ~66 mM) (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature on Slack activation properties.

claim: The [Na+]in at resting states (~10 mM) is much lower than the [Na+]in needed for effective Slack activation.
source: However, previous investigations have shown that the [Na+]in at resting states (~10 mM) is much lower than the [Na+]in needed for effective Slack activation (e.g., Kd value) (Kameyama et al., 1984; Zhang et al., 2010; Budelli et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on intracellular sodium concentrations.

claim: Native Slack channels need to localize with Na+ sources within a nanodomain to be activated and exert physiological function.
source: Therefore, native Slack channels need to localize with Na+ sources within a nanodomain to be activated and exert physiological function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the discrepancy between resting [Na+]in and the Kd for Slack activation.

claim: Slack channels are known to be functionally coupled with sodium-permeable ion channels in neurons, such as voltage-gated sodium (NaV) channels and AMPA receptors.
source: Slack channels are known to be functionally coupled with sodium-permeable ion channels in neurons, such as voltage-gated sodium (NaV) channels and AMPA receptors (Budelli et al., 2009; Hage and Salkoff, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Slack channel coupling.

claim: All neuronal NaV channels significantly sensitized Slack to 30 μM quinidine blockade.
source: Interestingly, all neuronal NaV channels significantly sensitized Slack to 30 μM quinidine blockade, whereas no effect was observed upon co-expression of Slack with GluA1, GluA2, GluA3, or GluA4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: No effect on Slack's sensitivity to quinidine blockade was observed upon co-expression of Slack with GluA1, GluA2, GluA3, or GluA4.
source: Interestingly, all neuronal NaV channels significantly sensitized Slack to 30 μM quinidine blockade, whereas no effect was observed upon co-expression of Slack with GluA1, GluA2, GluA3, or GluA4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: NaV1.6 sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade by nearly 100-fold (IC50 = 85.13 μM for Slack expressed alone and an IC50 = 0.87 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6).
source: When co-expressing Slack with NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells, NaV1.6 sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade by nearly 100-fold (IC50 = 85.13 μM for Slack expressed alone and an IC50 = 0.87 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6) (Figure 1A, B, D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, B, D and F.

claim: NaV1.6 exhibited greater than tenfold selectivity in sensitizing Slack to quinidine blockade against NaV1.1, NaV1.2, and NaV1.3.
source: NaV1.6 also exhibited greater than tenfold selectivity in sensitizing Slack to quinidine blockade against NaV1.1, NaV1.2, and NaV1.3 (Figure 1C and F, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and F, and Supplementary file 1a.

claim: Co-expression of the cardiac sodium channel NaV1.5 with Slack resulted in only an approximately threefold sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: When we co-expressed the cardiac sodium channel NaV1.5 with Slack, we observed only an approximately threefold sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: The apparent functional coupling between Slack and NaV channels is NaV-channel-subtype-specific, with NaV1.6 being particularly impactful in Slack's responsivity to quinidine blockade.
source: These results together indicate that the apparent functional coupling between Slack and NaV channels is NaV-channel-subtype-specific, with NaV1.6 being particularly impactful in Slack's responsivity to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential sensitization effects of different NaV channel subtypes.

claim: Co-expression of Slick and NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells resulted in a sensitization of Slick to quinidine blockade (sevenfold).
source: We next assessed whether NaV1.6 sensitizes Slick to quinidine blockade and observed that, similar to Slack, co-expression of Slick and NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells resulted in a sensitization of Slick to quinidine blockade (sevenfold) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: NaV1.6 can sensitize KNa channels to quinidine blockade in vitro.
source: These results support that NaV1.6 regulates both Slack and Slick and that NaV1.6 can sensitize KNa channels to quinidine blockade in vitro.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing sensitization of both Slack and Slick.

claim: 3 μM quinidine significantly inhibited native IKNa (44%) in wild-type neurons.
source: Notably, 3 μM quinidine significantly inhibited native IKNa (44%) in wild-type neurons (Figure 1I and K) and this inhibitory effect was not limited to targeting the larger IKNa (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I and K.

claim: 3 μM quinidine had no significant effect on IKNa in NaV1.6-knockout (NaV1.6-KO) neurons.
source: Conversely, the same concentration of quinidine had no significant effect on IKNa in NaV1.6-knockout (NaV1.6-KO) neurons (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J and K.

claim: NaV1.6 is required for the observed high sensitivity of native KNa channels to quinidine blockade.
source: These results support that NaV1.6 is required for the observed high sensitivity of native KNa channels to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from NaV1.6 knockout neurons.

claim: In HEK293 cells expressing Slack alone, 100 nM TTX did not affect Slack currents.
source: In HEK293 cells expressing Slack alone, 100 nM TTX did not affect Slack currents; nor did it affect Slack's sensitivity to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 83.27 μM) (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: In HEK293 cells expressing Slack alone, 100 nM TTX did not affect Slack's sensitivity to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 83.27 μM).
source: In HEK293 cells expressing Slack alone, 100 nM TTX did not affect Slack currents; nor did it affect Slack's sensitivity to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 83.27 μM) (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Upon co-expression of Slack and NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells, bath application of 100 nM TTX significantly reduced the effects of NaV1.6 in sensitizing Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 25.04 μM).
source: In contrast, upon co-expression of Slack and NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells, bath application of 100 nM TTX significantly reduced the effects of NaV1.6 in sensitizing Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 25.04 μM) (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Sodium influx through NaV1.6 contributes to NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: These findings support that sodium influx through NaV1.6 contributes to NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data using TTX to block sodium influx.

claim: Inactivating INaT reduced whole-cell Slack currents by 20%.
source: Consistent with previous investigations (Budelli et al., 2009; Hage and Salkoff, 2012), inactivating INaT reduced whole-cell Slack currents by 20%, and blocking INaP reduced Slack currents by 40% at +100 mV (Figure 2C, D, F and G), supporting that NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx activates Slack.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C, D, F and G.

claim: Blocking INaP reduced Slack currents by 40% at +100 mV.
source: Consistent with previous investigations (Budelli et al., 2009; Hage and Salkoff, 2012), inactivating INaT reduced whole-cell Slack currents by 20%, and blocking INaP reduced Slack currents by 40% at +100 mV (Figure 2C, D, F and G), supporting that NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx activates Slack.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C, D, F and G.

claim: NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx activates Slack.
source: Consistent with previous investigations (Budelli et al., 2009; Hage and Salkoff, 2012), inactivating INaT reduced whole-cell Slack currents by 20%, and blocking INaP reduced Slack currents by 40% at +100 mV (Figure 2C, D, F and G), supporting that NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx activates Slack.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduction of Slack currents when sodium influx is blocked.

claim: Inactivating INaT resulted in a >20-fold decrease in Slack's sensitization to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 22.26 μM).
source: Interestingly, inactivating INaT resulted in a >20-fold decrease in Slack's sensitization to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 22.26 μM) (Figure 2C and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and E.

claim: Blocking INaP had no effect on Slack's sensitization to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 1.60 μM).
source: In contrast, blocking INaP had no effect on Slack's sensitization to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 1.60 μM) (Figure 2F and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and H.

claim: NaV1.6 sensitizes Slack to quinidine blockade via INaT but not INaP.
source: These findings indicate that NaV1.6 sensitizes Slack to quinidine blockade via INaT but not INaP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing differential effects of inactivating INaT versus blocking INaP.

claim: NaV1.1, NaV1.2, NaV1.3, NaV1.5, and NaV1.6 exhibited similar levels of quinidine sensitivity (IC50 values in the range of 35.61–129.84 μM).
source: We used whole-cell patch-clamping to assess the sensitivity of NaV1.1, NaV1.2, NaV1.3, NaV1.5, and NaV1.6 to quinidine blockade. These sodium channels exhibited similar levels of quinidine sensitivity (IC50 values in the range of 35.61–129.84 μM) (Figure 2I and J and Supplementary file 1b), all of which were at least 40-fold lower than the NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I and J and Supplementary file 1b.

claim: Co-expressing Slack with NaV1.1, NaV1.2, NaV1.3, NaV1.5, or NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells did not change the sensitivity of these NaV channel subtypes to quinidine blockade.
source: Additionally, co-expressing Slack with NaV1.1, NaV1.2, NaV1.3, NaV1.5, or NaV1.6 in HEK293 cells did not change the sensitivity of these NaV channel subtypes to quinidine blockade (Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 1b.

claim: Differential quinidine affinity for specific NaV channel subtypes cannot explain the large observed NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: Thus, differential quinidine affinity for specific NaV channel subtypes cannot explain the large observed NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing similar quinidine sensitivity across NaV channel subtypes.

claim: NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade is directly mediated by INaT, rather than through some secondary effects related to NaV1.6's higher sensitivity to quinidine blockade.
source: Moreover, it is clear that NaV1.6-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade is directly mediated by INaT, rather than through some secondary effects related to NaV1.6's higher sensitivity to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing similar quinidine sensitivity across NaV channel subtypes and the specific role of INaT.

claim: NaV1.2 and NaV1.6 were localized to the axonal initial segment (AIS) of neurons.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Hu et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2017), NaV1.2 and NaV1.6 were localized to the axonal initial segment (AIS) of neurons, evident as the co-localization of NaV and AnkG, a sodium channel-associated protein known to accumulate at the AIS (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and citations to prior literature.

claim: Slack channels were localized to the AIS of neurons.
source: Slack channels were also localized to the AIS of these neurons (Figure 3A), indicating that Slack channels are located in close proximity to NaV1.6 channels, and supporting their possible interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Slack channels are located in close proximity to NaV1.6 channels.
source: Slack channels were also localized to the AIS of these neurons (Figure 3A), indicating that Slack channels are located in close proximity to NaV1.6 channels, and supporting their possible interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-localization of Slack and NaV1.6 at the AIS.

claim: NaV1.6 was co-immunoprecipitated with Slack in homogenates from mouse cortical and hippocampal tissues.
source: Moreover, NaV1.6 was co-immunoprecipitated with Slack in homogenates from mouse cortical and hippocampal tissues and from HEK293T cells co-transfected with Slack and NaV1.6 (Figure 3B and C), supporting that Slack and NaV1.6 form protein complexes in mouse brains.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: NaV1.6 was co-immunoprecipitated with Slack in homogenates from HEK293T cells co-transfected with Slack and NaV1.6.
source: Moreover, NaV1.6 was co-immunoprecipitated with Slack in homogenates from mouse cortical and hippocampal tissues and from HEK293T cells co-transfected with Slack and NaV1.6 (Figure 3B and C), supporting that Slack and NaV1.6 form protein complexes in mouse brains.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Slack and NaV1.6 form protein complexes in mouse brains.
source: Moreover, NaV1.6 was co-immunoprecipitated with Slack in homogenates from mouse cortical and hippocampal tissues and from HEK293T cells co-transfected with Slack and NaV1.6 (Figure 3B and C), supporting that Slack and NaV1.6 form protein complexes in mouse brains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Positive FRET signals were detected in cells co-expressing NaV1.6-mVenus and Slack-mTFP1, indicating a Slack-NaV1.6 interaction.
source: Upon imaging the emission spectra cells co-expressing NaV1.6-mVenus and Slack-mTFP1 (measured at the plasma membrane region) (Figure 3E), we detected positive FRET signals, indicating a Slack-NaV1.6 interaction (Figure 3F and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, F and H.

claim: Slack channels reside in close spatial proximity (less than 10 nm) to NaV1.6 channels in living cells.
source: The plasma membrane regions from HEK293T cells co-transfected with NaV1.6 and Slack showed FRET efficiency values much larger than a negative control (in which standalone mVenus and mTFP1 proteins were co-expressed) (Figure 3G and H), indicating that Slack channels reside in close spatial proximity (less than 10 nm) to NaV1.6 channels in living cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the FRET efficiency data.

claim: Slack increased the rate of recovery from fast inactivation of NaV1.6.
source: Slack increased the rate of recovery from fast inactivation of NaV1.6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E), with no significant effects on the steady-state activation, steady-state fast inactivation, or ramp currents (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, D and F and Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4E.

claim: Slack had no significant effects on the steady-state activation, steady-state fast inactivation, or ramp currents of NaV1.6.
source: Slack increased the rate of recovery from fast inactivation of NaV1.6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E), with no significant effects on the steady-state activation, steady-state fast inactivation, or ramp currents (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, D and F and Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, D and F and Supplementary file 1c.

claim: NaV1.6 had no significant effects on the activation rate or the current–voltage (I–V) relationship of Slack currents.
source: Additionally, we found that NaV1.6 had no significant effects on the activation rate or the current–voltage (I–V) relationship of Slack currents (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and B.

claim: The physical interaction between Slack and NaV1.6 produces functional consequences.
source: These results indicate that the physical interaction between Slack and NaV1.6 produces functional consequences.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing effects of Slack on NaV1.6 recovery from inactivation.

claim: When expressing Slack alone, increasing the sodium concentration did not sensitize Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 120.42 μM).
source: When expressing Slack alone, increasing the sodium concentration did not sensitize Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 120.42 μM) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Upon co-expression of NaV1.6 and Slack, NaV1.6 significantly sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 2.91 μM) in inside-out patches.
source: However, upon co-expression of NaV1.6 and Slack, NaV1.6 significantly sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 2.91 μM) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Physical interaction between Slack and NaV1.6 is a prerequisite for sodium-influx-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: These results support that physical interaction between Slack and NaV1.6 is a prerequisite for sodium-influx-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from inside-out patches showing sensitization requires NaV1.6 co-expression.

claim: The N-terminus and C-terminus of NaV1.6 significantly enhanced the sensitivity of Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 31.59 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6's N-terminus and IC50 = 43.70 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6's C-terminus).
source: Whole-cell recordings from HEK293 cells co-expressing Slack with these NaV1.6 fragments revealed that the N-terminus and C-terminus of NaV1.6 significantly enhanced the sensitivity of Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 31.59 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6's N-terminus and IC50 = 43.70 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6's C-terminus); note that the inter-domain linkers had no effect (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The inter-domain linkers of NaV1.6 had no effect on Slack's sensitivity to quinidine blockade.
source: Whole-cell recordings from HEK293 cells co-expressing Slack with these NaV1.6 fragments revealed that the N-terminus and C-terminus of NaV1.6 significantly enhanced the sensitivity of Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 31.59 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6's N-terminus and IC50 = 43.70 μM for Slack upon co-expression with NaV1.6's C-terminus); note that the inter-domain linkers had no effect (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: NaV1.6's N- and C-termini each interact with Slack.
source: Subsequent co-immunoprecipitation and glutathione S-transferase (GST) pull-down assays of HEK293T cell lysates experimentally confirmed that NaV1.6's N- and C-termini each interact with Slack (Figure 4D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Co-expression of Slack, NaV1.6's N-terminus, and NaV1.6's C-terminus resulted in obvious sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade, with an IC50 of 2.57 μM in inside-out recordings.
source: And inside-out recordings using an [Na+]in of 140 mM showed that co-expression of Slack, NaV1.6's N-terminus, and NaV1.6's C-terminus resulted in obvious sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade, with an IC50 of 2.57 μM (Figure 4F), thus fully mimicking the aforementioned effects of full-length NaV1.6 (IC50 = 2.91 μM) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The binding of NaV1.6's N- and C-termini to Slack is required for NaV1.6's sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: These findings support that the binding of NaV1.6's N- and C-termini to Slack is required for NaV1.6's sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that NaV1.6 fragments can mimic full-length NaV1.6 effects.

claim: NaV1.5 exhibited significantly larger current amplitudes than NaV1.6.
source: It is worth noting that NaV1.5 exhibited significantly larger current amplitudes than NaV1.6 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The replacement of both the N-terminus and C-terminus of NaV1.5 with NaV1.6's N-terminus and C-terminus (namely NaV1.5/6NC) fully mimicked effects of NaV1.6 in sensitizing Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 1.13 μM).
source: The replacement of both the N-terminus (residues 1–131) and C-terminus (residues 1772–2016) of NaV1.5 with NaV1.6's N-terminus (residues 1–132) and C-terminus (residues 1766–1980) (namely NaV1.5/6NC) fully mimicked effects of NaV1.6 in sensitizing Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 1.13 μM) (Figure 4G–I).

claim: Replacement of NaV1.5's N-terminus with NaV1.6's N-terminus (namely NaV1.5/6N) fully mimicked the effects of NaV1.6 (IC50 = 1.18 μM).

claim: The observed differences between NaV1.5 and NaV1.6 in sensitizing Slack are unlikely to be attributed to NaV1.6's smaller sodium current amplitudes but involve NaV1.6's N-terminus.

These results suggest that the observed differences between NaV1.5 and NaV1.6 in sensitizing Slack are unlikely to be attributed to NaV1.6's smaller sodium current amplitudes but involve NaV1.6's N-terminus.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from chimeric channels.

claim: NaV1.5's C-terminus sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 37.59 μM).
source: Consistently, NaV1.5's C-terminus sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 37.59 μM), whereas NaV1.5's N-terminus had no effect on Slack sensitization (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: NaV1.5's N-terminus had no effect on Slack sensitization to quinidine blockade.
source: Consistently, NaV1.5's C-terminus sensitized Slack to quinidine blockade (IC50 = 37.59 μM), whereas NaV1.5's N-terminus had no effect on Slack sensitization (Figure 4C).

claim: NaV-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade was significantly attenuated upon the additional expression of Slack's C-terminus, but not of Slack's N-terminus.
source: In HEK293 cells co-expressing NaV and Slack, NaV-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade was significantly attenuated upon the additional expression of Slack's C-terminus, but not of Slack's N-terminus (Figure 5B and C), suggesting that Slack's C-terminus can disrupt the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction by competing with Slack for binding to NaV1.6.

claim: Slack's C-terminus can disrupt the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction by competing with Slack for binding to NaV1.6.
source: In HEK293 cells co-expressing NaV and Slack, NaV-mediated sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade was significantly attenuated upon the additional expression of Slack's C-terminus, but not of Slack's N-terminus (Figure 5B and C), suggesting that Slack's C-terminus can disrupt the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction by competing with Slack for binding to NaV1.6.

claim: The interaction between Slack's C-terminus and NaV1.6 is required for NaV1.6's sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.

claim: Each of the Slack pathogenic mutant variants K629N, R950Q, and K985N interacts with NaV1.6 in HEK293T cell lysates.
source: Considering that these three mutations are located in Slack's C-terminus, and recalling that Slack's C-terminus interacts with NaV1.6 (Figure 5D), we first used co-immunoprecipitation assays and successfully confirmed that each of these Slack mutant variants interacts with NaV1.6 in HEK293T cell lysates (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The examined Slack mutant variants exhibited no discernible impact on the amplitudes of NaV1.6 currents.
source: Subsequently, whole-cell recordings revealed that the examined Slack mutant variants exhibited no discernible impact on the amplitudes of NaV1.6 currents (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), while pharmacologically blocking NaV1.6 currents using bath application of 100 nM TTX significantly reduced the amplitudes of Slack mutant variant (SlackR950Q) currents (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting a Na+-mediated functional coupling between Slack mutant variant and NaV1.6 currents.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Pharmacologically blocking NaV1.6 currents using bath application of 100 nM TTX significantly reduced the amplitudes of Slack mutant variant (SlackR950Q) currents.
source: Subsequently, whole-cell recordings revealed that the examined Slack mutant variants exhibited no discernible impact on the amplitudes of NaV1.6 currents (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), while pharmacologically blocking NaV1.6 currents using bath application of 100 nM TTX significantly reduced the amplitudes of Slack mutant variant (SlackR950Q) currents (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting a Na+-mediated functional coupling between Slack mutant variant and NaV1.6 currents.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There is a Na+-mediated functional coupling between Slack mutant variant and NaV1.6 currents.
source: Subsequently, whole-cell recordings revealed that the examined Slack mutant variants exhibited no discernible impact on the amplitudes of NaV1.6 currents (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), while pharmacologically blocking NaV1.6 currents using bath application of 100 nM TTX significantly reduced the amplitudes of Slack mutant variant (SlackR950Q) currents (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting a Na+-mediated functional coupling between Slack mutant variant and NaV1.6 currents.

claim: NaV1.6 significantly sensitized all of the examined Slack mutant variants to quinidine blockade, with IC50 values ranging from 0.26 to 2.41 μM.

claim: NaV1.6 interacts with examined Slack mutant variants and sensitizes them to quinidine blockade.
source: These results support that NaV1.6 interacts with examined Slack mutant variants and sensitizes them to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation and functional studies.

claim: The Slack-NaV1.6 interaction contributes to the therapeutical role of quinidine in the treatment of KCNT1-related epilepsy.
source: It is plausible that the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction contributes to the therapeutical role of quinidine in the treatment of KCNT1-related epilepsy.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental data showing NaV1.6 sensitizes Slack mutants to quinidine.

claim: Blocking NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx significantly reduced Slack current amplitudes.
source: Having established that blocking NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx significantly reduced Slack current amplitudes (Figure 2D and G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we found that the heterozygous knockout of NaV1.6 significantly reduced the AHP amplitude in murine hippocampal neurons (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), together indicating that NaV1.6 activates native Slack through providing Na+.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The heterozygous knockout of NaV1.6 significantly reduced the AHP amplitude in murine hippocampal neurons.
source: Having established that blocking NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx significantly reduced Slack current amplitudes (Figure 2D and G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we found that the heterozygous knockout of NaV1.6 significantly reduced the AHP amplitude in murine hippocampal neurons (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), together indicating that NaV1.6 activates native Slack through providing Na+.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: NaV1.6 activates native Slack through providing Na+.
source: Having established that blocking NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx significantly reduced Slack current amplitudes (Figure 2D and G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), we found that the heterozygous knockout of NaV1.6 significantly reduced the AHP amplitude in murine hippocampal neurons (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), together indicating that NaV1.6 activates native Slack through providing Na+.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduction of Slack currents and AHP when NaV1.6 is blocked or knocked out.

claim: Disruption of the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction should reduce the amount of Na+ in the close vicinity of epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants and thereby counter the increased current amplitudes of these Slack mutant variants.
source: We therefore assumed that disruption of the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction should reduce the amount of Na+ in the close vicinity of epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants and thereby counter the increased current amplitudes of these Slack mutant variants.
evidence: This is speculation based on the understanding of the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction.

claim: Expression of Slack's C-terminus significantly reduced whole-cell current densities of SlackG269S and SlackR398Q in HEK293 cells co-expressing epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants and NaV1.5/6NC.
source: Pursuing this, we disrupted the Slack-NaV interaction by overexpressing Slack's C-terminus (to compete with Slack) and measured whole-cell current densities. In HEK293 cells co-expressing epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants (G288S, R398Q) (Rizzo et al., 2016; Barcia et al., 2019) and NaV1.5/6NC, expression of Slack's C-terminus significantly reduced whole-cell current densities of SlackG269S and SlackR398Q (Figure 7A and B), supporting that disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction can indeed reduce current amplitudes of Slack mutant variants, which may protect against seizures induced by Slack mutant variants.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction can reduce current amplitudes of Slack mutant variants.
source: In HEK293 cells co-expressing epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants (G288S, R398Q) (Rizzo et al., 2016; Barcia et al., 2019) and NaV1.5/6NC, expression of Slack's C-terminus significantly reduced whole-cell current densities of SlackG269S and SlackR398Q (Figure 7A and B), supporting that disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction can indeed reduce current amplitudes of Slack mutant variants, which may protect against seizures induced by Slack mutant variants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduction of mutant Slack currents by Slack's C-terminus.

claim: Disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction may protect against seizures induced by Slack mutant variants.
source: In HEK293 cells co-expressing epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants (G288S, R398Q) (Rizzo et al., 2016; Barcia et al., 2019) and NaV1.5/6NC, expression of Slack's C-terminus significantly reduced whole-cell current densities of SlackG269S and SlackR398Q (Figure 7A and B), supporting that disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction can indeed reduce current amplitudes of Slack mutant variants, which may protect against seizures induced by Slack mutant variants.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental data showing reduction of mutant Slack currents.

claim: Viral expression of SlackG269S resulted in faster seizure progression in mice compared to control GFP expression.
source: We assessed a time course of KA-induced seizure stages at 10 min intervals and found that viral expression of SlackG269S resulted in faster seizure progression in mice compared to control GFP expression (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: SlackG269S-expressing mice showed significantly higher seizure severity than GFP-expressing mice.
source: We calculated the total seizure score per mouse to assess seizure severity (Kim et al., 2021). SlackG269S-expressing mice showed significantly higher seizure severity than GFP-expressing mice (Figure 7F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The percentage of mice with stage VI–IX seizures increased from 9.1% in GFP-expressing control mice to 58.3% in the SlackG269S-expressing mice.
source: The percentage of mice with stage VI–IX seizures also increased, from 9.1% in GFP-expressing control mice to 58.3% in the SlackG269S-expressing mice (Figure 7G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Viral expression of SlackG269S significantly increases seizure susceptibility in mice.
source: These results support that viral expression of SlackG269S significantly increases seizure susceptibility in mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from the in vivo seizure model.

claim: Viral expression of Slack's C-terminus in SlackG269S-expressing mice significantly decreased seizure progression, seizure severity, and the percentage of mice experiencing stage VI–IX seizures.
source: To evaluate the potential therapeutic effects of disrupting the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction, we delivered two AAV9s (one for SlackG269S and one for Slack's C-terminus [residues 326–1238]) into the CA1 region of mice (Figure 7D). Viral expression of Slack's C-terminus in SlackG269S-expressing mice significantly decreased seizure progression, seizure severity, and the percentage of mice experiencing stage VI–IX seizures (Figure 7E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E–G.

claim: Viral expression of Slack's C-terminus can prevent SlackG269S-induced seizures in mice.
source: These results support that viral expression of Slack's C-terminus can prevent SlackG269S-induced seizures in mice, thus showcasing that using Slack's C-terminus to disrupt the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction is a promising therapeutic intervention to treat KCNT1-related epilepsy (Figure 8).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from the in vivo seizure model.

claim: Using Slack's C-terminus to disrupt the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction is a promising therapeutic intervention to treat KCNT1-related epilepsy.
source: These results support that viral expression of Slack's C-terminus can prevent SlackG269S-induced seizures in mice, thus showcasing that using Slack's C-terminus to disrupt the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction is a promising therapeutic intervention to treat KCNT1-related epilepsy (Figure 8).
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental data from the in vivo seizure model.

source: We here found that NaV1.6's N- and C- termini bind to Slack's C-terminus and sensitize Slack to quinidine blockade via NaV1.6-mediated transient sodium currents.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by multiple experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The pharmacological blocking effects of a channel blocker are not exclusively mediated by the channel per se, but modulated by channel's interacting proteins.

evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing NaV1.6 modulates Slack's sensitivity to quinidine.

claim: Slack and NaV1.6 form a channel complex.
source: Our results support that Slack and NaV1.6 form a channel complex, while also implying that NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx increases the Na+ concentration in the close vicinity of Slack to activate Slack.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation, FRET, and functional studies.

claim: NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx increases the Na+ concentration in the close vicinity of Slack to activate Slack.
source: Our results support that Slack and NaV1.6 form a channel complex, while also implying that NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx increases the Na+ concentration in the close vicinity of Slack to activate Slack.

claim: NaV1.6 has been reported to dominate the initiation and propagation of action potentials in AIS in excitatory neurons.
source: As a low-threshold NaV channel subtype, NaV1.6 has been reported to dominate the initiation and propagation of action potentials in AIS in excitatory neurons (Hu et al., 2009; Kole et al., 2008; Lazarov et al., 2018; Katz et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on NaV1.6 function.

claim: The activation of Slack by NaV1.6 at AIS has multiple impacts, including ensuring the timing of the fast-activated component of Slack currents, regulating the action potential amplitude, and apparently contributing to intrinsic neuronal excitability.
source: The activation of Slack by NaV1.6 at AIS has multiple impacts, including ensuring the timing of the fast-activated component of Slack currents, regulating the action potential amplitude, and apparently contributing to intrinsic neuronal excitability (Kaczmarek, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and citations to prior literature.

claim: GOF Slack mutant variants have been linked to a broad spectrum of epileptic disorders that are accompanied by intellectual disabilities and both psychomotor and developmental defects.
source: As previously mentioned, GOF Slack mutant variants have been linked to a broad spectrum of epileptic disorders that are accompanied by intellectual disabilities and both psychomotor and developmental defects (Cole et al., 2021; Gertler et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on KCNT1 mutations and epilepsy.

claim: Many patients with KCNT1-related epilepsy are refractory or nonresponsive to conventional anticonvulsants.
source: Given that many patients are refractory or nonresponsive to conventional anticonvulsants (McTague et al., 2018; Gertler et al., 1993; Fitzgerald et al., 2019), and considering the limited success of quinidine in clinical treatment of KCNT1-related epilepsy, inhibitors targeting Slack are needed urgently (Cole et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on treatment of KCNT1-related epilepsy.

claim: Inhibitors targeting Slack are needed urgently for KCNT1-related epilepsy.
source: Given that many patients are refractory or nonresponsive to conventional anticonvulsants (McTague et al., 2018; Gertler et al., 1993; Fitzgerald et al., 2019), and considering the limited success of quinidine in clinical treatment of KCNT1-related epilepsy, inhibitors targeting Slack are needed urgently (Cole et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on the limited success of current treatments.

claim: Several small-molecule inhibitors against Slack have been reported, providing informative starting points for drug development efforts with KCNT1-related epilepsy.
source: Several small-molecule inhibitors against Slack have been reported, providing informative starting points for drug development efforts with KCNT1-related epilepsy (Cole et al., 2020; Griffin et al., 2021; Spitznagel et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Slack inhibitors.

claim: The discovery of the Slack-NaV1.6 complex challenges the traditional view that Slack acts as an isolated target in KCNT1-related epilepsy.

evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing the importance of the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction.

claim: Co-expression of Slack and NaV1.6 in heterologous cell models should be performed when analyzing clinically relevant Slack mutations and when screening anti-epileptic drugs for use in treating KCNT1-related disorders.
source: Indeed, our study supports that co-expression of Slack and NaV1.6 in heterologous cell models should be performed when analyzing clinically relevant Slack mutations and when screening anti-epileptic drugs for use in treating KCNT1-related disorders.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experimental data showing the importance of the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction.

claim: ADSHE-related mutations are clustered in the regulator of conductance of K+ (RCK2) domain.
source: Genotype–phenotype analysis has shown that ADSHE-related mutations are clustered in the regulator of conductance of K+ (RCK2) domain; while EIMFS-related mutations do not show a particular pattern of distribution (Bonardi et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature on genotype-phenotype analysis.

source: Further, the epilepsy-related Slack mutant variants confer their GOF phenotypes through two molecular mechanisms: increasing maximal channel open probability (Pmax) or increasing sodium sensitivity (Kd) of Slack (Tang et al., 2016).

claim: The inhibitory effect of 3 μM quinidine on IKNa in wild-type neurons was not limited to targeting the larger IKNa.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: 100 nM TTX blocks NaV1.6-mediated sodium influx.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B and a citation to prior literature.

claim: 20 μM riluzole selectively blocked INaP compared to INaT in HEK293 cells co-expressing Slack and NaV1.6.
source: Our findings ultimately confirmed that the 20 μM riluzole selectively blocked INaP compared to INaT in HEK293 cells co-expressing Slack and NaV1.6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) and that 20 μM riluzole had no effect on Slack currents when expressed alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: 20 μM riluzole had no effect on Slack currents when expressed alone.
source: Our findings ultimately confirmed that the 20 μM riluzole selectively blocked INaP compared to INaT in HEK293 cells co-expressing Slack and NaV1.6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) and that 20 μM riluzole had no effect on Slack currents when expressed alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: There is a possibility of a hypothetical open conformation of Slack that brings its quinidine binding pocket into a high-affinity state when modulated by INaT.
source: We speculate that with physical modulation by NaV1.6, INaT may elicit a specific open conformation of Slack that brings its quinidine binding pocket into a high-affinity state, which could lead to a substantial increase in Slack's sensitivity to quinidine blockade.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental data showing differential effects of INaT and INaP.

claim: There are multiple open conformations of Slack.
source: The possibility of this hypothetical open conformation is supported by previous reports of the presence of subconductance states detected in single-channel recordings of Xenopus oocytes expressing Slack channels (Brown et al., 2008), which implies that there are multiple open conformations of Slack.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature on Slack channel properties.

claim: Riluzole has been reported to bind to Slack channels with low affinity.
source: Additionally, it is worth noting that blocking of INaP by application of riluzole has its limitation on selectivity. Riluzole has been reported to bind to Slack channels with low affinity (Biton et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature on riluzole binding.

claim: The dual binding of riluzole to both Slack and NaV1.6 may stabilize or inhibit the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction, consequently influencing the sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
source: Therefore, the dual binding of riluzole to both Slack and NaV1.6 may stabilize or inhibit the Slack-NaV1.6 interaction, consequently influencing the sensitization of Slack to quinidine blockade.
